stocks.discussion_driver: Best Buy surged ~3% after reporting its strongest comparable sales growth in five years (+6.1% YoY), with Q3 FY2027 earnings and revenue topping analyst expectations. The beat arrives perfectly timed ahead of Black Friday and the holiday electronics season, with management raising its full-year EPS outlook to $11.40–$12.25.
bull_case: Best-in-class comp sales recovery (+6.1% YoY) signals durable consumer demand for electronics; tariff refunds boosted EPS by an estimated $0.15/share and may continue as a tailwind
Black Friday and holiday season provide near-term revenue catalyst; raised full-year guidance gives management credibility and reduces downside earnings risk
bear_case: Stock is trading above most analyst consensus price targets (~$95.64), implying limited near-term upside; Goldman Sachs maintains a Sell rating with an $89 target, citing structural concerns
Consumer electronics is a discretionary category vulnerable to spending pullbacks; competitive pressure from Amazon and big-box retailers constrains pricing power and margin expansion

stocks.discussion_driver: Autodesk fell ~3% on November 25 despite beating Q3 FY2027 earnings (EPS $3.20 vs $3.07 est.) and raising Q4 guidance, a classic buy-the-rumor sell-the-news reaction after shares had already rallied into the print. The result itself was solid: strength in AEC (architecture, engineering, construction) driven by civil infrastructure and data center demand, plus robust large-enterprise renewals.
bull_case: Q3 FY2027 EPS beat with raised Q4 guidance; RBC (Outperform, $305), BTIG (Buy), and Rosenblatt (Buy, $375) all maintained positive ratings; 32-analyst consensus target of $317 implies ~27% upside from current levels
AI-integrated design tools and exposure to long-cycle infrastructure buildouts (data centers, civil engineering) provide durable, subscription-based revenue growth well into 2027 and beyond
bear_case: Stock fell on earnings day despite the beat, signaling that expectations were already elevated; Cantor Fitzgerald initiated at Neutral with a $215 target — the lowest on the Street — citing stretched valuation

Trading at ~33x trailing earnings; the bull case depends on a significant expansion in profitability that has not yet fully materialized; broad tech selloff risk in a rising-rate or AI-skeptic environment
